title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #7

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the letter E stand for on a compass rose? (1 mark)
   A. Edge
   B. Equator
   C. Earth
   D. East

2. Which is the correct way to write the in-between point that is between south and west? (1 mark)
   A. South-west
   B. Sowest
   C. West-south
   D. West-south-west

3. What does a compass needle point to? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. The nearest town
   C. South
   D. North

4. On most maps, which direction is at the top? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. North
   C. West
   D. South

5. Which county has a neighbouring county called Kiambu to its north? (1 mark)
   A. Turkana
   B. Kisumu
   C. Nairobi
   D. Mombasa

6. A pupil says that a county with many people must be the biggest in area. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Counties never have people
   B. Area and population are different things
   C. People make land bigger
   D. Only farms make counties big

7. On the county map in the lesson, the neighbour drawn on the right side is in which direction from the county? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. West
   C. East
   D. North

8. What is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. A road
   C. A building made by people
   D. A natural feature on the surface of the Earth

9. What is a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A natural forest
   B. A river
   C. A new shopping mall
   D. A place built long ago that tells us about the past

10. Why can no person do every job alone? (1 mark)
   A. Money is not needed
   B. There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   C. People are lazy
   D. Jobs are not important

11. Which group depends on teachers? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers
   B. Everyone who wants to learn
   C. Only farmers
   D. Only drivers

12. Who helps at weddings and funerals in many communities? (1 mark)
   A. Only the police
   B. Only the government
   C. Neighbours and relatives
   D. Nobody

13. On a dot map, what does a group of many dots close together show? (1 mark)
   A. An empty area
   B. A road
   C. A crowded area
   D. A river

14. What is population? (1 mark)
   A. The rainfall in a place
   B. The number of animals in a place
   C. The size of a place
   D. The number of people living in a place

15. Which is a good school rule? (1 mark)
   A. Fight in class
   B. Come to school on time
   C. Break desks
   D. Write on walls

16. What should you do if you break a school rule? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Say sorry and accept fair guidance
   C. Run away
   D. Blame others

17. On a timeline, which event comes first? (1 mark)
   A. The oldest event
   B. The biggest event
   C. The funniest event
   D. The newest event

18. Where might you see a school motto? (1 mark)
   A. On a rain cloud
   B. In a river
   C. On the badge or gate
   D. In the sky

19. Who can tell you about the history of your school? (1 mark)
   A. The headteacher or teachers who have been there long
   B. A shop
   C. A stranger who has never visited
   D. A random person

20. Why must children not do hard or dangerous work? (1 mark)
   A. It is fun
   B. It harms their health and schooling
   C. It makes them stronger
   D. It is a school rule

21. Which is a way of conserving forests? (1 mark)
   A. Building fires
   B. Planting more trees than we cut
   C. Cutting all trees
   D. Burning the forest

22. Which of these is a natural resource? (1 mark)
   A. A road
   B. Water in a river
   C. A school building
   D. A tractor

23. Which item of clothing protects a worker's head in a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Helmet
   B. Sandals
   C. Scarf
   D. Skirt

24. Where are fish processing factories found? (1 mark)
   A. In the sky
   B. On top of Mount Kenya
   C. In a desert without water
   D. On the shores of Lake Victoria

25. Which of these helps drivers to see pupils on the road? (1 mark)
   A. Reflective strips
   B. A hat that covers the eyes
   C. A black bag
   D. Dark clothes

26. What does Stop-Think-Share teach? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore rules
   B. Think before you post
   C. Share your password
   D. Post quickly

27. In an essay on good citizenship, what should the beginning say? (1 mark)
   A. A recipe
   B. A list of foods
   C. The weather report
   D. What a good citizen is

28. What is cyberbullying? (1 mark)
   A. Playing a computer game
   B. Writing a letter
   C. Reading a book
   D. Using phones or computers to hurt or frighten someone

29. Which of these is a good digital citizen habit? (1 mark)
   A. Asking an adult before going online
   B. Sending mean messages
   C. Talking to strangers
   D. Sharing passwords

30. What is the Kiswahili word for peace? (1 mark)
   A. Chakula
   B. Rafiki
   C. Shule
   D. Amani

31. Which of these is a way of living in peace with others? (1 mark)
   A. Teasing
   B. Sharing what you have
   C. Cheating
   D. Grabbing things

32. What is child trafficking? (1 mark)
   A. Adopting children legally
   B. Taking children on a picnic
   C. Taking children away by trick or force to make money from them
   D. Taking children to school

33. Which of these is a benefit of democracy in school? (1 mark)
   A. Everyone has a voice
   B. Only some pupils are heard
   C. Leaders are never checked
   D. Pupils are ignored

34. A candidate gives sweets for votes. What is this? (1 mark)
   A. Fair campaigning
   B. Kindness
   C. Cheating
   D. Democracy

35. What does a patron do? (1 mark)
   A. Cooks for pupils
   B. Drives the bus
   C. Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   D. Wins all elections

36. Why is it important for leaders to have good qualities? (1 mark)
   A. Resources are wasted
   B. People trust them and live in peace
   C. People fear them
   D. People quarrel

37. What do clan elders do? (1 mark)
   A. Repair roads
   B. Keep customs and settle disputes
   C. Cook school lunch
   D. Sell tickets

38. What happens when leaders are dishonest? (1 mark)
   A. People are happier
   B. Trust is lost and resources are wasted
   C. The community grows faster
   D. Nothing changes

39. Which best describes the difference between the governor and an MCA? (1 mark)
   A. The governor makes laws
   B. An MCA is above the governor
   C. They do the same job
   D. The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor

40. Who elects the governor? (1 mark)
   A. The chief
   B. The president alone
   C. Registered voters in the county
   D. The teachers

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Draw a side view of the land showing a mountain, a valley and a plain and label them. (5 marks)

42. Name three child rights. (3 marks)

43. A dot map has 1 dot for every 1,000 people. A town has 12 dots and a dry area has 2 dots. How many more people live in the town? Show your working. (3 marks)

44. Explain how the four seasons can influence what people do in your county. Give one example for each season. (5 marks)

45. Give three ethical practices in managing a school enterprise. (3 marks)

46. Name the four seasons in the county. (2 marks)

47. Give three reasons why economic activities are important. (3 marks)

48. List the steps for solving a conflict peacefully. (4 marks)

49. Write a short poem of four lines about the benefits of industries in your county. (5 marks)

50. What is a majority? (2 marks)

51. Give two reasons why farmers plant crops at the start of the rainy season. (2 marks)

52. Give five people who serve your community and say how each helps. (5 marks)

53. Describe how a losing candidate should behave and why. (3 marks)

54. Explain why some cultural practices are no longer kept. (3 marks)

55. List four questions you could ask to find out the history of your school. (4 marks)

56. A group spent Ksh 350 on seeds and Ksh 150 on tools. They sold vegetables for Ksh 800. Find the profit. Show working. (3 marks)

57. Give three ways of conserving natural resources. (3 marks)

58. Why do people trade? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — East
   E is the short form of east.

2. A — South-west
   We say the north or south word first, so it is south-west.

3. D — North
   A magnetic compass needle always turns to point north.

4. B — North
   Maps are drawn with north at the top unless a north arrow shows otherwise.

5. C — Nairobi
   Kiambu lies to the north of Nairobi County.

6. B — Area and population are different things
   Size is about area. Population is the number of people.

7. C — East
   When north is at the top, the right side is east.

8. D — A natural feature on the surface of the Earth
   Physical features such as mountains and rivers are natural.

9. D — A place built long ago that tells us about the past
   Historic built places are old places made by people.

10. B — There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   Nobody can grow all food, teach, heal and build alone.

11. B — Everyone who wants to learn
   Teachers help children learn to read and write, which everybody needs.

12. C — Neighbours and relatives
   People help by cooking, lending items and comforting.

13. C — A crowded area
   Many dots show many people.

14. D — The number of people living in a place
   Population is the number of people in an area.

15. B — Come to school on time
   Being punctual is a good habit.

16. B — Say sorry and accept fair guidance
   We should be honest and accept correction.

17. A — The oldest event
   Timelines run from oldest to newest.

18. C — On the badge or gate
   Mottos are often on badges and gates.

19. A — The headteacher or teachers who have been there long
   Reliable people and records give true information.

20. B — It harms their health and schooling
   Child labour is harmful and against the law.

21. B — Planting more trees than we cut
   Replanting keeps the forest alive.

22. B — Water in a river
   Water in a river is from nature.

23. A — Helmet
   Helmets protect workers' heads.

24. D — On the shores of Lake Victoria
   Fish are processed near the lake where they are caught.

25. A — Reflective strips
   Reflective strips shine in light.

26. B — Think before you post
   We should think about whether it is true, kind and safe.

27. D — What a good citizen is
   The introduction gives the main idea.

28. D — Using phones or computers to hurt or frighten someone
   Cyberbullying is bullying online.

29. A — Asking an adult before going online
   Asking permission keeps you safe.

30. D — Amani
   Amani means peace.

31. B — Sharing what you have
   Sharing shows kindness.

32. C — Taking children away by trick or force to make money from them
   Trafficking is a crime.

33. A — Everyone has a voice
   Democracy makes everyone heard.

34. C — Cheating
   Buying votes is unfair.

35. C — Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   The patron is a teacher adviser.

36. B — People trust them and live in peace
   Good leaders build trust and peace.

37. B — Keep customs and settle disputes
   Clan elders guard customs and settle quarrels.

38. B — Trust is lost and resources are wasted
   Dishonesty harms the community.

39. D — The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor
   They have different roles.

40. C — Registered voters in the county
   Voters in the county elect the governor.

SECTION B
----
41. (5 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with a high peak labelled mountain, a low dip labelled valley and a flat area labelled plain.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct shape drawn and 1 mark for each label, up to 5 marks.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The right to education, to health care and to protection. Accept food, a name or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each right.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000 more people.
   Working / marking points: 12 x 1,000 = 12,000; 2 x 1,000 = 2,000; 12,000 - 2,000 = 10,000. 1 mark for each step.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Rainy: farmers plant crops. Dry: farmers harvest and dry crops. Hot: people drink more water and wear light clothes. Cold: people wear warm clothes and drink hot tea. Award a fifth mark for a clear explanation of why seasons matter for farming.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each season example and 1 mark for the link to activities.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Be honest with money and customers, be fair in sharing work and rewards, and care for the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each practice.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hot, cold, dry and rainy.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for all four, 1 mark for two or three.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: They provide food, they give jobs and income, and they earn taxes for county services.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stop, calm down, talk and listen, find a solution together, and say sorry and forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step, up to 4.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: A poem that mentions jobs, income and goods, is neat and rhymes or has rhythm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four lines, 1 mark for jobs, 1 mark for income or goods, 1 mark for a title, 1 mark for correct language.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: The larger number of votes, more than any other choice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for larger number, 1 mark for votes.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rain gives the seeds water to grow, and the wet soil is soft to dig.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer grows food, teacher teaches, nurse treats the sick, driver carries people and goods, trader sells goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each person with a correct service.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Accept the result peacefully, congratulate the winner and offer to help. This keeps peace and shows respect for democracy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some practices harm people, such as female genital mutilation and early marriage. The law forbids them. We keep the good parts and leave out the harmful ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harm, 1 mark for law, 1 mark for keeping good parts.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: When was the school started? Who started it? Who was the first headteacher? How has the school changed?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each relevant question.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 300.
   Working / marking points: Cost = 350 + 150 = 500. Profit = 800 - 500 = 300. 1 mark for cost, 1 mark for subtraction, 1 mark for answer.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plant trees, save water, and reduce waste by reusing and recycling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: People trade to get the goods they need but cannot make, and to earn money from the goods they produce.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
